messages:
sarah_support: Heads-up — Customer ACCT-4982 opened a ticket saying they get 403 "Invalid API key" when calling /v1/embeddings. They are on Starter plan and haven't rotated keys. Support console logs show our entitlement check failing just before the auth check. Can eng help triage?

jlee: Can you paste the request-id, region, and a curl repro? Also which SDK/version?

sarah_support: Repro below from customer (region: us-west1). Request-id: req_0a7c3f. SDK: python-sdk v1.2.1.
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_ABC123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"test","model":"tiny-embed-1"}'
```
Response: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Body: {"error":"invalid_api_key"}
Headers: X-Request-ID: req_0a7c3f, X-Region: us-west1

Server log (filtered):
```
time=2026-02-18T14:22:11Z level=info msg=\"entitlement_check\" account=ACCT-4982 feature=embeddings result=missing
time=2026-02-18T14:22:11Z level=warn msg=\"entitlement_gate\" account=ACCT-4982 code=403 mapped_error=invalid_api_key
```

sarah_support: Customer is getting told their key is invalid so they tried rotating keys which broke some app flows. We need to avoid this misleading UX.

mmartin: Thanks — this looks like a mapping bug in the gateway that converts entitlement denial into the generic invalid-key error. The entitlement service returns gated=true but our edge layer currently maps any 403 from the policy check to the auth error payload for backward compatibility. That makes plan/billing gating indistinguishable from bad creds.

mmartin: Short-term: we should change the response body when entitlement is the cause to include a clear subcode, e.g. {"error":"feature_not_enabled","reason":"plan_entitlement","feature":"embeddings"} and keep 403. Long-term: add a distinct substatus header like X-Auth-Reason or WWW-Authenticate: Entitlement realm=\"plan\".

vikas_infra: I can push a tiny hotfix to the gateway mapping to surface a subcode. Will open PR to stop rewriting the message. Patch should be low-risk: adjust mapping in middleware from return generic_auth_error() to return entitlement_error(subcode). Target ETA ~4h (can bump to urgent if needed).

ops-bot: Created internal ticket T-5891: "Entitlement gates returned as invalid_api_key — misleading 403" assigned to eng-gateway.

accounts_team: FYI — we've seen 3 other Starter accounts file the same symptom since the last pricing change. They all tried rotating keys and that caused additional churn. Can support surface a caution in the UI while we patch?

jlee: Workaround for now in support reply: explain that the key is valid, this is a plan limitation; include steps to verify via org API that embeddings feature flag=false and suggest temporary upgrade/demo entitlement if they need emb. Do we have an API check string we can paste?

mmartin: Yes, use the org features endpoint:
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_ABC123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/ACCT-4982/features
# returns {"embeddings": false, "chat": true, ...}
```
So reply template: "We see your API key authenticates, but embeddings are not enabled on your plan. To enable embeddings please upgrade or request a trial. If you want us to validate your key without plan gating, reply and we can run a diagnostic."

sarah_support: Drafted reply and sent to customer. Marking ticket P1 for the mapping change. Keeping thread open for the deploy.

vikas_infra: PR up in 10m, will run canary to us-west1 first. I will post back on success/failure.

jlee: Thanks — once hotfix is live we should also add an observability metric (entitlement_denied -> auth_masked_count) so we can catch regressions.

sarah_support: Noted. I'll keep monitoring customer replies and escalate if they request immediate workaround.

mmartin: Follow-up action items: 1) hotfix gateway mapping (vikas) 2) support UI message for entitlements (accounts_team) 3) add metric and rule (jlee/mmartin) 4) postmortem if we see churn > 5 orgs.

sarah_support: Closing loop for now — will update thread with deploy status. :thumbsup:
